date: c. 304-311 (approx.; dating not verified in the sources I read)
translator_edition: William Fletcher, ANF vol. 7 (Buffalo 1886), public domain; text read on New Advent (Books IV, V, VI). Translator credit verified on the page.
original_edition: Latin text read on Latin Wikisource transcriptions (la.wikisource.org/wiki/Divinae_institutiones/Liber_IV, Liber_V, Liber_VI). The printed edition behind the transcription is not stated in the page I read; the standard critical editions are CSEL 19 (Brandt-Laubmann, 1890) and the Teubner (Heck-Wlosok, in progress), not checked here.
authenticity_note: genuine (no dispute raised in the sources read)
notes: ANF chapter numbers differ from the Latin section numbers by one chapter in Book V (Latin V.19 = ANF V.20; Latin V.20 = ANF V.21). Book VI matches (Latin VI.20 = ANF VI.20). The scripture references in ANF VI.18 ('Romans 12:19; Hebrews 10:30') are editorial and are NOT in the Latin (Latin VI.18.11 has no citation); see summary.

notes: Chapter numbering follows the Fletcher text: LIV = 'Of the freedom of religion in the worship of God'. The EWTN page carries some OCR artefacts (e.g. 'be-haft'); avoid those words in quotes. Footnote markers such as '(1)' appear inside the text.

title_es: Sobre la muerte de los perseguidores
title_en: Of the Manner in Which the Persecutors Died
translator_edition: William Fletcher (ANF vol. 7), public domain; credit verified on the New Advent page read.
original_edition: Latin text on thelatinlibrary.com/lactantius/demort.shtml (read in part, 'Liber ad Donatum confessorem de mortibus persecutorum'); the edition is not stated on the page. Chapter 47 and 48 Latin not located in the text read.
authenticity_note: generally ascribed to Lactantius; I did not check the scholarly debate on authorship
notes: Used only for the X (adverse) check: it celebrates divine punishment of persecutors. The Edict of Milan appears in ch. 48 as reported by Lactantius (edict text, not his own voice).
